papers.title: Spatial-Temporal Vision Transformers for Robust Quadruped Locomotion in Rugged Terrains
papers.abstract: Quadrupedal robot locomotion over complex non-flat terrain requires agile dynamic balancing under visual latency and partial observability. However, existing reinforcement learning policies frequently fail when crossing unstructured rocky obstacles due to depth sensor noise. In this paper, we propose ST-LocoViT, a spatial-temporal vision transformer that integrates exteroceptive depth streams with proprioceptive IMU history. Unlike prior frame-by-frame policies, our key innovation is a causal token recurrence module operating at 50 Hz on edge compute. Extensive field evaluations across rocky trails show a 94.2% traverse completion rate, outperforming previous blind and height-map baselines by 27.5%. This demonstrates practical sim-to-real transfer for autonomous planetary and search-and-rescue robotics.

In this paper, we propose ST-LocoViT, a spatial-temporal vision transformer that integrates exteroceptive depth streams with proprioceptive IMU history. Unlike prior frame-by-frame policies, our key innovation is a causal token recurrence module operating at 50 Hz on edge compute. Extensive field evaluations across rocky trails show a 94.2% traverse completion rate, outperforming previous blind and height-map baselines by 27.5%. This demonstrates practical sim-to-real transfer for autonomous planetary and search-and-rescue robotics.

insights.problem: Quadrupedal dynamic balancing over irregular terrain suffers from visual latency and sensory noise.
insights.approach: Spatial-temporal vision transformer fusing depth cameras with 50 Hz proprioceptive history.
insights.key_innovation: Causal token recurrence mechanism for real-time edge processing without high-power GPUs.
insights.results: Achieved 94.2% traverse completion rate on real physical quadrupeds, a 27.5% gain over baselines.
insights.applications: Search-and-rescue robots, planetary surface exploration, and hazardous industrial inspection.
insights.limitations: Requires pre-calibrated camera mounting and assumes dry ground friction characteristics.

papers.title: MicroQuant: Sub-Milliwatt Deep Learning Inference for Distributed Edge IoT Sensor Nodes
papers.abstract: Edge artificial intelligence on battery-less or solar-powered IoT microcontrollers is severely restricted by strict sub-milliwatt power envelopes and tight SRAM constraints. Current quantization techniques often introduce non-negligible classification degradation. To overcome this fundamental bottleneck, we develop MicroQuant, an ultra-low-bit mixed-precision quantization methodology. Our approach couples gradient-free weight compression with an assembly-optimized SIMD inference runtime. Hardware measurements on ARM Cortex-M4 confirm sub-0.8 mW active consumption with an 8.4x reduction in RAM footprint while preserving 98.7% of floating-point accuracy. This framework unlocks long-term remote acoustic and environmental monitoring at scale.
papers.summary: Edge artificial intelligence on battery-less IoT microcontrollers is severely restricted by sub-milliwatt power envelopes. To overcome this fundamental bottleneck, we develop MicroQuant, an ultra-low-bit mixed-precision quantization methodology. Our approach couples gradient-free weight compression with an assembly-optimized SIMD inference runtime. Hardware measurements on ARM Cortex-M4 confirm sub-0.8 mW consumption with an 8.4x RAM reduction while preserving 98.7% accuracy. This framework unlocks long-term remote environmental monitoring.

insights.problem: Severe SRAM and power boundaries on energy-harvesting IoT microcontrollers prevent neural net execution.
insights.approach: Mixed-precision non-uniform quantization coupled with custom assembly integer execution kernels.
insights.key_innovation: Gradient-free compression that avoids resource-heavy backpropagation during edge adaptation.
insights.results: Sub-0.8 mW power draw and 8.4x memory reduction with negligible accuracy degradation (<1.3%).
insights.applications: Wildlife tracking collars, smart agriculture acoustic sensors, and industrial vibration diagnostics.
insights.limitations: Targeted primarily at 32-bit ARM Cortex architectures; requires architectural recompilation for RISC-V.

papers.title: Autonomous Multi-Agent Task Allocation in Partially Observable Industrial Environments
papers.abstract: Coordinating decentralized fleets of autonomous warehouse robots under partial visibility and intermittent wireless dropouts presents significant combinatorial complexity. Existing centralized dispatchers suffer from single-point failure modes. We introduce ConsensusNet, a distributed multi-agent reinforcement learning architecture featuring localized peer-to-peer auction protocols. In simulated trials and physical factory floor validation, ConsensusNet achieved zero deadlocks across 10,000 order cycles while reducing fleet idle time by 31.4% compared to standard rule-based heuristic dispatchers.
papers.summary: Coordinating decentralized fleets of autonomous warehouse robots under partial visibility presents significant combinatorial complexity. In physical factory floor validation, ConsensusNet achieved zero deadlocks across 10,000 order cycles while reducing fleet idle time by 31.4% compared to standard heuristic dispatchers.

insights.problem: Warehouse dispatching breaks down when central network access drops or robots encounter unmapped congestion.
insights.approach: Distributed peer-to-peer auction consensus built on graph neural message passing.
insights.key_innovation: Fully decentralized coordination with proven deadlock avoidance guarantees without a central coordinator.
insights.results: Zero deadlocks across 10,000 simulated and physical order dispatch cycles with a 31.4% idle-time drop.
insights.applications: Automated fulfillment centers, port container haulage, and multi-drone delivery networks.
insights.limitations: Communication overhead scales quadratically if local agent density exceeds 50 units in close proximity.
